main_mystery: Can Nadia Cole execute Victor Rhodes and escape justice, or will her own buried first kill surface and destroy everything she built?
truth: Nadia Cole is the executioner. She kills guilty men the system failed to punish. Victor Rhodes is her current target — he is not only guilty of the murder she's investigating, but he has figured out her true nature and is building a case against her, including evidence of her very first kill (Julian Croft). The two-way hunt ends with Rhodes's death, but his dead-man's-switch surfaces the first-kill evidence to an unknown third party, leaving Nadia on a leash.

red_herrings.description: A detective (unaffiliated with Rhodes) begins circling Nadia's network after a suspicious death is flagged — the reader is led to believe this detective will expose Nadia, but the thread fizzles when the detective is reassigned or the case is dropped by a higher authority.
red_herrings.note: This is a false alarm — the detective is a red herring to raise tension in Act 2, but the real threat is Rhodes's counter-investigation.

red_herrings.description: A rival podcaster starts digging into Nadia's past, hinting at a 'dark secret' — the reader suspects the rival will uncover the first kill, but the rival's investigation is a dead end (they find nothing concrete).
red_herrings.note: This red herring misdirects the reader from Rhodes's more dangerous investigation.

red_herrings.description: Priya Anand's medical examiner office is audited, suggesting her altered records might be discovered — but the audit is routine and reveals nothing, a false alarm that tests Nadia's paranoia.
red_herrings.note: This red herring builds tension around the network's vulnerability but is a dead end.

major_reveals.description: Nadia's origin wound: Mara Cole's murder and Julian Croft's walk free, establishing why Nadia kills.
major_reveals.note: Partial reveal — not the full first-kill details, but the emotional foundation.

major_reveals.description: The network is introduced: Sasha Okafor, Priya Anand, Wren Delgado — each with a role and a secret.
major_reveals.note: Establish the network early so the betrayal hurts later.

major_reveals.description: Victor Rhodes is not a passive target — he has figured out Nadia is the executioner and is building a case against her.
major_reveals.note: This is the Act 1 end reveal that flips the narrative from hunter to hunted.

major_reveals.description: The network betrayal: one of the three (Sasha, Priya, or Wren) leaks information to Rhodes or an outside party, causing a major setback for Nadia.
major_reveals.note: The betrayer is decided at plan time and kept consistent. This reveal must hurt — loyalty was built before the break.

major_reveals.description: Full origin reveal: Nadia's first kill — Julian Croft, killed in a staged boating accident — is shown in detail, including the emotional and procedural weight.
major_reveals.note: This is the emotional climax of the origin thread. Must be fully paid off here, not earlier.

major_reveals.description: Rhodes's dead-man's-switch: after his death, evidence of Nadia's first kill surfaces to an unknown third party, setting up the Book 2 hook.
major_reveals.note: This is the final reveal — the ticking bomb that survives Rhodes's death.

clues.description: Nadia's thumb-tap tic is noticed by a listener in a podcast comment, but dismissed as a nervous habit — a subtle clue to her methodical nature.
clues.note: This clue is a character marker that pays off in the origin reveal when Nadia's cold precision is fully shown.

clues.description: A boating accident report from three years ago mentions Julian Croft's death — the report is clean, but a detail (e.g., the fuel line was tampered) is buried in the fine print.
clues.note: This is the first seed of Nadia's first kill. The reader may not recognize it until the origin reveal.

clues.description: Victor Rhodes leaves a voicemail for Nadia that sounds like a casual fan message, but the wording is too precise — he uses a phrase from her private notes, not her podcast.
clues.note: This clue triggers the Act 1 end reveal that Rhodes knows her true nature.

clues.description: A deleted search history on Rhodes's computer shows he researched 'podcaster + unsolved murder + boating accident' — linking him to Julian Croft's case.
clues.note: This clue shows Rhodes's counter-investigation is deeper than Nadia realizes.

clues.description: Nadia's sister Mara's diary entry (found in a box) mentions a 'developer who came to the house' — a reference to Julian Croft, planting the origin connection.
clues.note: This clue is emotional — it humanizes the origin wound before the full reveal.

clues.description: Priya Anand's signature on a death certificate is slightly different from her usual handwriting — a clue that she altered the record.
clues.note: This clue is a red herring seed (RH03) but also a genuine vulnerability in the network.

clues.description: A photograph of Julian Croft's yacht shows a fuel line that looks recently replaced — a visual clue to the staged accident.
clues.note: This is a visual clue that pays off in the origin reveal.

clues.description: A text message from an unknown number to Rhodes contains details about Nadia's private schedule — only a network member would know this.
clues.note: This clue is the first concrete evidence of the network betrayal.

clues.description: Wren Delgado's encrypted file access logs show an unusual download at 3 AM — a clue that the hacker may be the leak, or that someone else is using Wren's credentials.
clues.note: This clue points to the betrayer but leaves room for misdirection (it could be a frame).

clues.description: Rhodes's attorney's office receives a sealed envelope with instructions to release it upon his death — the dead-man's-switch trigger.
clues.note: This clue is planted in Act 3 to set up the Book 2 hook.

clues.description: A flash drive found in Rhodes's safe contains a single file: 'JULIAN CROFT — BOATING ACCIDENT — FULL REPORT' with annotations that link the accident to Nadia.
clues.note: This is the final clue — the evidence that survives Rhodes's death and becomes the Book 2 hook.
